mutantRecords.name: M1: a NEW undeclared orphan is reported by the inventory predicate
M2: a declared orphan that is actually wired is reported (the list cannot rot into an allowlist)
M3: an absent verify:m55 is reported by the C6 predicate
M4: the root scan is load-bearing — a root-less core leaves the delegated gate unwired
M5: an extra root (a closure-gate body) opens a dependency the npm scripts do not
M6: a source-named, unwired, undeclared verifier is reported by the protection predicate
M6b: the same verifier stops being reported once it is wired (the check is not unconditional)
M7: an empty reason is reported by the triage predicate
M7b: a real stated reason is not reported (the triage is not unconditional)
M8: only the verified-over-non-verified pair drifts (the predicate discriminates)
M9: a REAL planted orphan file is seen by the live census and refused by G1

limitations: Reachability is derived by parsing package.json script strings and closure-gate source text for `script/…` references. A gate invoked by a mechanism this parser does not model (a shell script, a CI workflow file, a Makefile, a `.mjs` runner that spawns by computed path) would be reported as an orphan. Every declared orphan in the baseline therefore carries a stated reason, and the baseline is the review surface for that judgement.
The G5 ledger-vs-disk check reads `status` from each record; a lane whose governance gate never writes its manifest is only reported, not corrected, by this gate.
This gate reports; it does not repair. Wiring a gate into package.json and projecting a ledger are lane-owner actions.
